prerequisites: Knowledge of Fundamentals of Mechanical Engineering and Specific Mechanical Technology
Calculation, Design and Testing of Machines

learning_outcomes.text: The student will know and apply the fundamentals of Computer-Aided Engineering in problems of deformable solids, heat transfer, fluid dynamics, explicit dynamics, and modal analysis.
Applied knowledge of Computer-Aided Engineering in problems of deformable solids, heat transfer, fluid dynamics, explicit dynamics, and modal analysis.
Applied knowledge of advanced techniques for machine calculation and design.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Oral and written communication in one's own language.
Information management skills (ability to search for and analyze information from diverse sources).

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the Finite Element Method
Introduction to the Finite Element Method
Primitive method for interpolation of the motion field
Shape functions of Lagrangian and serendipity elements
Variational Formulation of the Finite Element Method
Variational formulation of the state equation
Conditions of displacement functions and convergence criteria
Errors, recovery processes, and error estimators
assessment_rules: The overall grade will be the weighted average of the grades obtained in the recoverable and non-recoverable assessment tests. A minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required on the written test to pass the course; otherwise, the final grade will be a fail, capped at 4.5 points. A minimum attendance of 90% in laboratory and computer practices is required for the 'Practice reports and memoirs' assessment component to be counted. Fraudulent completion of an assessment test will result in a 0 for that test and a final grade of 0 for the course in that examination session.
